newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher on light holiday volumes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher on light holiday volumes.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended higher Monday, on light volumes, with the London Metal Exchange (LME) still closed for the Easter holidays and some New York metals trading desks still out also.
Both COMEX and the LME were also closed Friday.
COMEX May copper ended up 1.05 cents at 112.85 cents a pound, after trading a 111.30-113.20 cent range on estimated total COMEX copper volume of 7,000 lots.
"The fundamentals still look good, but I'm not sure how long that's going to last with production expected to pick up later this year," one trader said.
Resistance is still seen around last week's high at 113.20 cents and the contract high at 114.50 cents seen on March 7, but the four-month old rally still looks to have some momentum, traders said.
The COMEX May/July spread remains firmly backwardated around 3.55 cents, while the COMEX/LME arbitrage remains in COMEX's favor by around 3.00 cents in the May contract.
The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data for the period ended March 25, released late Friday, showed the funds remaining heavily net long by 12,339 contracts.

The low level of global refined copper stocks, representing only about three weeks of consumption, combined with potential labor unrest, at the Polish KGHM Polska Miedz operation and at the U.S. Phelps Dodge Chino mine, continued to support copper prices, traders said.

Better-than-expected activity in the U.S. housing and auto sectors in recent data suggests good gains in copper consumption in 1997, though a supply surplus is still expected later in the year, analysts said.
